Downlands Community School Values: We care. We share. We believe. We achieve.
Welcome to our School
Downlands Community School lies at the heart of Blandford Camp, enjoying an extremely safe and friendly environment for the children and extensive grounds for sports and playtime. Our unique situation means that many of our pupils change schools frequently, so we take great pride in ensuring that every child settles in quickly and happily, both educationally and socially.
We are a friendly primary school catering for children aged 3 to 11, offering a broad and balanced curriculum alongside extra opportunities which will stimulate your child’s curiosities and passions.
James Rielly – Headteacher

Headteacher’s Welcome
I warmly welcome you to our school website and I sincerely hope that you are able to find the information you need. Nevertheless, my colleagues and I are always happy to speak over the phone or in person so please do get in touch if you need to know more.
I was appointed as Headteacher of Downlands Community School in September 2019 and this is my 2nd headship. Having worked in Dorset schools for 28 years in a variety of settings, it is with some authority that I am able to tell you that this school is a unique educational setting. Being only one of four schools to be situated ‘behind the wire’ of a military base, this is perhaps an obvious statement. Indeed, the vast majority of children have parents from the armed services and our school community is very lucky to have a wealth of experience, knowledge and leadership skills from within this special community.
Downlands School is one of only four schools to be situated ‘behind the wire’ and serves a diverse and international armed forces community.
Downlands is proud of its national and internationally diverse school community. Visitors to the school will experience a range of regional accents from all corners of the United Kingdom. We are also lucky to serve a diverse and international armed forces community and we have particularly strong links as regards Nepalese families.
Downlands Community School is an all-through Primary, taking children from three years old as part of our Dandelions Preschool. Indeed, the preschool setting is located next to our Reception class and together they form our EYFS unit, creating the best possible start for our children.
Allowing children to settle quickly, feel welcome and make friends is of huge importance to us. Many of our pupils have a highly mobile educational life due to the nature of their parents’ careers within the armed services. Therefore, it is fundamentally important that we quickly establish safe and trusting relationships with children and their families. I am very proud of my team here at Downlands and can confidently say that every staff member is totally committed to the cause of children attending our school. As our motto states: We Care. We Share. We Believe. We Achieve.
I am very happy to talk to existing or prospective parents about any questions they may have about Downlands Community School. Please take advantage of my weekly drop-in service on Fridays between 0930 and 1015hrs. Alternatively, make an appointment with my colleagues in the office and I would be happy to find the time for you.
Mr James Rielly – Headteacher

Prospective Parents
Whilst we hope that you can find plenty of information on our website, we would urge all prospective parents to get in touch with the school (see contacts page) to get some expert guidance from the office team or to arrange a conversation with Headteacher or Assistant Headteacher. We welcome school viewings as we believe that our school sells itself, but it will also give you the opportunity to ask any questions you might have and see the learning environment for yourself.
Whilst we welcome an initial conversation about the school admission process, all formal school admissions submissions must be made via this Dorset Council Website. Children may only start attending the school once officially on roll. We will also ask you to complete a school registration form (see below) for internal enrollment purposes.
For parents serving in the armed forces, you may find it helpful to look at the CEAS Guide to Moving Schools for further information.

Before & After School Clubs
Here at Downlands, we offer a Breakfast Club and After School Care. Breakfast Club is open from 7.45 am until 8.40 am when the children are taken to their respective classes. For their breakfast we offer them a wide choice of cereals and toast, fresh fruit is always available for them throughout the session. We encourage the children to tidy up after themselves once they have finished eating. Breakfast is included in the cost of the morning session.
All of the resources within the school are available for us to use and benefit from. Our enthusiastic team plan a variety of activities to suit all different types of interest. Snack for after school club is served at 3:30 PM and is included in the costs below. You may opt-out of this scheme and supply your child with a snack and drink but we request that it is healthy.
The cost for these sessions are :
3.15pm pick up (preschool only) £2.50
4.00pm pick up £5.00
5.00pm pick up £10.00
Please feel free to talk to Mrs Cress Cooper for further information or if you would like to secure a place for your child.

Governors
The school is served by a team of governors who offer a range of experiences, skills and perspectives. The role of school governor is increasingly important in modern education and a strong governing body is needed to offer support and challenge in equal measure so that our overall standards are kept as high as possible. Downlands Community School Governing Body meet every month under a ‘single meeting structure’, whereby all matters (school improvement, finance, staffing, premises) are appraised by all Governors. Mathematics
At Downlands Community School, we believe that mathematics is an essential skill that enables us to make sense of the world around us. Through discussion, reasoning and recognising that making mistakes is part of our learning journey, children will become confident problem solvers. Daily mathematics lessons will ensure our pupils develop their core math skills, whilst developing their key fluency and number skills. All our pupils will have the opportunity to learn through a CPA (Concrete, Pictorial and Abstract) approach and have the opportunity to develop a wide range of strategies to solve real life problems.
Downlands Community School is a maintained school within Dorset Local Authority, therefore we will follow the Primary National Curriculum. We are on a journey as a school community developing a mastery approach to mathematics. The following policy describes the vision and pedagogical principles for teaching and learning mathematics, which has been agreed by staff and governors.
